KEY MESSAGE 1...More summer-like conditions return tomorrow. 
Rain chances return late Sunday.

Dry and sunny conditions with some diurnal cu continue through the 
rest of today. Dew points remain in the 40s and 50s across the 
region through tonight as well with lows in the 50s and low 60s. 925 
mb temperatures remain generally around 15C as well before 
increasing slightly to around 18-20C tomorrow with high pressure 
starting to shift more to the east and SW winds kicking in. Highs 
tomorrow return to the low to mid 80s along with slightly increased 
humidity.

Latest guidance continued to indicated a weak low pressure moving 
close to the region, emphasizing chance for rain generally south of 
I-90 Sunday night. It's worth noting, though, that showers do remain 
possible across all of southern New England starting in the late 
evening hours. There's a low chance for some embedded thunder, but 
that is generally relegated to the south coast and the southern 
waters. Not anticipating much of a washout with these. Higher 
confidence that showery conditions continue overnight Sunday towards 
the south coast, clearing out heading into Monday morning. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Backdoor cold frontal boundary Monday brings 
onshore flow, decreased cloud cover and cooling afternoon 
temperatures. 

Monday looks to be the least-active of the upcoming workweek, but it 
still features a backdoor cool front slipping SW from coastal NH/ME 
early in the day, then continuing on SW and tending to stall 
somewhere near southwest CT or southern NY late in the day. 
Considerable cloudiness to start then gives way to increasing NE 
winds, decreased cloud cover and temps either hovering or slowly 
cooling off. Though temps should reach the low 80s in western MA/CT, 
midday highs in the mid/upper 70s eastern MA and RI then cool off to 
the low/mid 70s by sundown. Cloud cover then increases Mon night but 
should still end up dry for the most part, though rain chances 
increase into the pre-dawn hours. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Unsettled Tuesday through Thursday with several
opportunities for showers and thunderstorms, with a chance for 
some to become strong in western MA and CT. Timing which days 
may have better storm chances is still uncertain. 

Tue through Thurs look more active/unsettled, as the backdoor 
frontal boundary stalls from SW to NE through NY State and the 
northeast fringe of a substantial heat ridge centered over the Ohio 
Valley by Tue tries to build into the northern mid-Atlantic and 
perhaps into a small portion of Southern New England. This places 
Southern New England between a more stable and seasonable airmass to 
the northeast and a warm/hot, humid and conditionally unstable 
airmass to our southwest. Above the stalled sfc boundary lies a belt 
of strong NW flow aloft (e.g. 300 mb winds approaching 100 kt), 
which tends to favor shortwave energy impulses moving SE along the 
stalled front. Several opportunities for showers and thunderstorms 
seem likely in this period, but the details of which are uncertain. 
Those hinge on the exact placement/evolution of the frontal 
boundary, if we can tap into the more unstable air to our southwest, 
and the timing of shortwaves in the strong NW flow aloft. Machine-
learning guidance from the GEFS and Colorado State show some severe 
weather potential for our western/southwest counties in this period, 
and SPC highlights a small sliver of western Hampden County and 
western/central Hartford County in a 15% probability for severe 
weather for Wednesday, uncommon for what is a Day-5 forecast. Am 
skeptical we get entrenched into the more unstable air to our 
southwest but the best potential for doing so would more likely be 
south and west of Worcester. Something that we'll need to monitor as 
we get into the mesoscale model range. PoPs are pretty high given 
the medium-range nature of the forecast for the Tue thru Thurs 
timeframe, in the 30-60% range. Temperatures were kept in the 70s to 
low 80s Tue thru Thurs, with rather mild lows in the mid 60s (climo 
low temperature values are in the upper 50s/around 60).
